subject: Preflight: LumenForge dedicated capacity — elasticity checklist & thresholds
messages:
From: Diego Ramos <diego.ramos@lumenforge.ai>

Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@lumenforge.ai>

Subject: LumenForge preflight: Q4 capacity planning and thresholds

Jordan —

Thanks again for the quick intro last week. We're ramping toward a private Dedicated deployment in Q4 and want to do a preflight sizing/ops review before the SOW. High level expectations:
- Peak concurrent sessions: 1.2k (chat-heavy; median seq len ~256, 95p ~1024)
- Expected sustained tokens/day at peak week: ~45M/day
- Burst characteristics: recurring short spikes ~10-12 minutes, 3x baseline, 2–3x per hour during release windows
- Business ask: minimize committed reserved capacity while guaranteeing <200ms median gen latency for our primary customer workflow

Attached is our traffic projection workbook and a short notes doc. We'd like to confirm:
1) Suggested reserved slab and a recommended ephemeral/shoulder policy to avoid big upfront commits
2) Eviction and fallback model guidance if reserved is saturated
3) How billing/credits work for transient burst beyond commit

Can you loop in whoever owns Dedicated sizing and any runbook owners — we want this to be reviewable by our infra and platform teams this week.

Best,
Diego Ramos
Head of Platform Engineering
LumenForge

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Diego Ramos <diego.ramos@lumenforge.ai>

Subject: RE: LumenForge preflight: Q4 capacity planning and thresholds

On Mon, Nov 16, 2026 at 10:03 AM Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com> wrote:
> Ben/Karthik: please review the workbook and propose a slab + shoulder approach that keeps your latency target while lowering up-front reserve.

Diego/Priya — thanks for the projections. Quick summary of our recommendation after a first pass through the numbers:

1) Baseline reserved slab
- Start with a conservative reserve equivalent to ~420 simultaneous GPU sessions (N1 slab equivalent) to cover steady-state + short sustained peaks; this maps to ~60% of your projected median QPS under typical token lengths.

2) Ephemeral shoulder pool (pre-authorized transient capacity)
- Provision a separate transient pool equal to 1.0x the reserved slab (so +420 session-equivalent capacity) that can be consumed on short notice for bursts. This pool is pre-authorized for billing and will be drained preferentially before we scale the reserved slab.
- Charge model: metered usage with per-minute granularity; 20% premium over reserved token unit price for transient minutes. Alternatively, apply burst credits that amortize across quarter.

3) Auto-raise thresholds and cooldowns
- Trigger scale-up into the shoulder pool when 3-minute rolling utilization of reserved slab >72% AND 95p tail latency exceeds 250ms.
- Maintain a minimum cooldown of 8 minutes after a scale-up to avoid flapping; require 20 consecutive minutes of utilization <40% to scale the shoulder pool down.

4) Fallback/eviction behavior
- Priority: reserved slab traffic > shoulder > preemptible best-effort. Preemptible tasks will receive best-effort queueing and will be evicted when cluster-level safe headroom reaches <10% for 4 consecutive minutes.
- For critical SLO traffic we recommend model-fallback to a smaller quantized variant to preserve latency under extreme saturation.

5) Observability & guardrails
- Per-request token-level latency and cost tagging, early warning alert at 65% sustained reserved utilization for >10 minutes, and a runbook link to initiate short-term crediting/contract amendments if spikes repeat.

I've attached a short preflight checklist (redwood-preflight-checklist.pdf) that lists the operational items we want validated on your side before cutover. We can tune numbers after the call but this gives you a pragmatic starting posture that aims to reduce commit while protecting latency.

Ben Carter
Director, Solutions Architecture | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-preflight-checklist.pdf
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@lumenforge.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: LumenForge preflight: Q4 capacity planning and thresholds

Ben — thanks, this is helpful and concrete. A couple clarifying questions from our infra team:

- The 420-session reserved slab: what GPU instance class does that map to (e.g., A10G equivalents, or smaller multi-model instances)? We need an ops-ready mapping for procurement.
- For the ephemeral pool: can we set a hard quarterly cap (credits) so our committed spend stays within forecast?
- For model-fallback: how fast can Redwood flip to a quantized variant and what's the expected delta in token quality / throughput?

Also, can you (Ben/Karthik) put together a very short ops appendix that includes the exact eviction priorities, how we surface preemptible job IDs in logs, and the billing reconciliation flow for burst credits?

We should aim to sign-off on the preflight checklist in the sync today so our procurement team can prep the SOW.

—Priya Shah
Head of SRE | LumenForge
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@lumenforge.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: RE: LumenForge preflight: Q4 capacity planning and thresholds

On Tue, Nov 17, 2026 at 11:05 AM Priya Shah <priya.shah@lumenforge.ai> wrote:
> Ben — thanks, this is helpful and concrete. A couple clarifying questions from our infra team:

Good questions — quick answers and an ops appendix outline below. We'll attach the appendix to the SOW pack after your sign-off.

1) GPU mapping
- 420 session-equivalents maps to the following nominal build: 12 x G5.2xlarge equivalent nodes (each node mapped to ~35 session-equivalents given your median sequence length and model token mix). We'll include exact instance SKU mappings per cloud provider in the appendix.

2) Quarterly cap / credits
- Yes: we can pre-define a quarterly burst credit pool. Example structure: purchase X burst credits covering up to 250 ephemeral-hours for the quarter at a 10% discount vs metered transient pricing. Any usage beyond credits billed at the metered premium. We will include a simple reconciliation clause for end-of-quarter true-up.

3) Model fallback latency/quality delta
- We can bake a fallback policy that routes to a 4-bit quantized variant as first fallback. Typical observed delta: 6–9% quality delta on our internal evals for open models of the same family; latency improves ~25–40% depending on batch packing. We'll include eval snapshots for the exact model pair in the appendix so you can baseline expected behavior.

4) Ops appendix (outline):
- Exact eviction priority ordering and signal thresholds (cluster headroom, per-node memory, kv-cache pressure)
- Log surfacing: ephemeral job IDs prefixed with LF-EPH for easy filtering; a Kibana dashboard link template
- Billing reconciliation: daily metering export to a secured bucket, weekly aggregated invoice preview, and quarter-end true-up flow
- Escalation contacts and SLA exception window (2-hour emergency scaling request path)

Next steps I suggest:
- Jordan: confirm if we should draft the appendix as an addendum to the SOW or keep as a separate runbook artifact.
- Diego/Priya: if the quarter-burst-credit approach looks good I can put a sample credit schedule on HubSpot for review.

I'll drop the detailed appendix PDF into the Drive link and update the HubSpot record.

Karthik Iyer
Principal Product Manager, Capacity | Redwood Inference
